title: IMD issues orange alert for very heavy rainfall over South Interior Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry & Karaikal - News On AIR
article_text:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an orange colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall over South Interior Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal today. Heavy rainfall is also expected over Andhra Pradesh, Coastal Karnataka, Kerala and Mahe during the next two days. According to IMD, the Southwest monsoon withdrew from the entire country yesterday.

It added that the Northeast monsoon rainfall activity has commenced over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Rayalaseema, South Interior Karnataka, Kerala and Mahe. Meanwhile, IMD has forecast a generally cloudy sky with a spell of light rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning at many places in the National Capital during early morning to noon today. According to the Weather Agency, the maximum temperature in the National Capital will be around 29 to 31 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature will hover around 18 to 20 degrees Celsius today.

The Met Department also predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Haryana, Chandigarh, Uttarakhand, East Rajasthan and West Uttar Pradesh today. Similar weather conditions are also expected over Madhya Pradesh, Telangana, Odisha and Lakshadweep during the next two days. Meanwhile, hot and humid weather conditions are likely to prevail over Konkan and Goa today.

Srikanth of Chennai Rains (COMK) said coastal Tamil Nadu and South Andhra Pradesh are likely to receive rainfall from later today. Winds are expected to shift to easterly-northeasterly directions, triggering convergence over Delta districts and adjoining northern Tamil Nadu. The next two to three days could bring typical Northeast Monsoon conditions, with Chennai likely to receive night and early morning showers.
